title: ASSAY-1 Measured Grade Certificate
description: A machine-readable, signed attestation of a measured (Tier-3) grade for one fleet with respect to one workload class, per ASSAY-1 v0.1 §8.3. Designed to be referenced by a contract (a lender covenant, an EFP delivery term, a procurement requirement) via its certificate_id + ledger inclusion proof, rather than a marketing page. Every field a counterparty relies on is either measured or a disclosed caveat — never inferred.

certificate_id.description: e.g. ASSAY-CERT-2026-7QX4K2. The hash a contract references.

fleet_id.description: The registry fleet identifier this certificate attests.

source_class.description: THE honesty field. 'first-party-assay' = the registry rented and measured the fleet itself. 'operator-submitted' = the operator ran the open harness on their own metal and signed the output; the registry verified the signature, nonce, and §8.2 disclosures, NOT the metal. Both are measured (unlike a disclosure grade); their independence differs and is stated here, on the certificate.

workload_class.description: A grade is meaningful only w.r.t. a workload class (§0.1, §4). No context-free grade.

measured_grade.description: Substitutability grade (§5) computed from the MEASURED metrics below for this workload class — not from disclosures.

assurance_tier.description: Measured = Tier 3 (§7). Anything below is a disclosure grade and does not get a certificate.

primary_metric.description: The measured number the grade rests on. For W1/W3 (training/scale-out) this is DCB (§3.3).

line_rate_reference.description: Vendor-published line rate for the same allocation, if any — for the efficiency ratio.

delivered_over_line_rate.description: value / line_rate_reference. The DCB story: >=0.9 excellent, 0.5-0.9 real-but-note-the-gap, <0.5 red flag (§8, first-harness-run.md).

secondary_metrics.description: Optional additional probes once the harness ships them (alltoall, csd-probe, checkpoint-burst, serving-latency). Same {name,value,unit} shape.

measurement_window.description: n=1 honesty: a certificate attests THIS window, not the fleet in general (§10.2). Re-certification resamples.

tenancy.description: §8.2 anti-gaming disclosures, recorded on the certificate so a reader sees the conditions, not just the number.

concurrent_tenants.description: Tenants sharing the fabric during the run. null = not declared (itself a finding).

examples: 16 GPU / 2 node — the max this self-serve product sells as one unit

allocation_equals_max_sellable.description: True iff the measured allocation equals the largest the operator will actually sell (§8.2 — no golden-slice benchmarking). False must be explained in notes.

run_nonce.description: Registry-issued, time-bounded token that makes the run Verified-eligible (§8.2). Absent nonce → not a certificate, ingests as self-reported.

expires_utc.description: Decay is a first-class term (§7): a measured grade expires 90 days after the measurement window without re-run. A contract references the certificate WITH its expiry — a lapsed certificate is a covenant event, not a silent staleness.

ledger.description: Inclusion proof in the public measurement ledger (docs/measurement-ledger.md). This is what makes the certificate un-backdatable and verifiable without trusting the registry.

record_sha256.description: sha256 of the harness output file (matches the harness's own sha256 field).

ots_proof_path.description: OpenTimestamps .ots proof anchoring the record to Bitcoin block time.

signatures.description: Published GPG fingerprints; verify against ComputeAssay/measurements KEYS.md.

registry_fingerprint.description: The registry key that issued/countersigned this certificate.

operator_fingerprint.description: Present for source_class=operator-submitted: the operator's key that signed the raw run.

notes.description: Any caveat a reader must see: software stack date, single-node-only limitation, why allocation_equals_max_sellable is false, resampling commitment, etc.
